_comment: The three beats of an ally's arc (Expansion 6 F.1, docs/ADVENTURES.md §5.6; game/story/stakes.py offers them on a night at camp or at the inn): the confidence (their stake, told by the fire), a crisis (revenge: they want to go now; doubt: they want to go home; taken: one who rides with the patron is carried off), and the fate (when the tale is won and they live: their oath, or home). The op 'ally' moves their arc (told, held, held_hard, breaks, home, taken, sworn, farewell); the condition 'party_room' asks for a place in your company. Words: the tale's, with {ally}, {ally_full}, {stake}, {mine}, {confidence} and the ally's {they} {them} {their} {They} {Their} {s} {are} {have}.

title: What {ally} came for
By the fire
{ally}'s reason
text: The fire is low and the others are asleep. {ally} has been sitting up, not sleeping, and at last speaks, quietly, as if to the embers.
{ally} has said little since {they} joined you. Tonight, with the watch half over, {they} sit{s} down beside you, and stay{s} there.
It is late, and cold, and {ally} hands you a cup of something hot that you did not ask for. Then {they} stay{s}, and you understand {they} {have} something to say.

label: Listen, and say nothing.
result: You let the silence be. After a while {ally} nods, as if you had answered, and goes to {their} blanket.
You say nothing, and it seems to be the right thing. {ally} sleeps, that night, for the first time in days.
Neither of you says anything more. In the morning {ally} walks beside you, not behind.

label: Promise {them} it will be paid for.
result: "Paid for," {ally} says. "Aye. I'll hold you to that." {They} mean{s} it.
{ally} looks at you a long while. "Don't promise what you can't do," {they} say{s}. "But I'll take it. I'll take it."
"That's all I wanted to hear," {ally} says, and wipes {their} face, and goes to sleep.

label: Tell {them} grief makes poor company on a hard road.
result: {ally} stares at you, and then gets up without a word. In the morning {they} {are} civil, and nothing more.
"Aye," {ally} says. "I'll keep it to myself, then." And {they} keep{s} it.
{ally} laughs, not kindly. "You're a cold one. Well. Cold is what the work wants, maybe."

title: {ally} will not wait
Now, or never
The knife by the fire
text: You wake in the dark to find {ally} already up, armed, {their} pack on {their} shoulder. "I'm going now," {they} say{s}. "Tonight. I've waited long enough for {mine}, and every day we wait it lives."
{ally} has heard something on the road today, and has not spoken since. At the fire {they} stand{s} up at last. "I'm done waiting. I'm going up there, to {home}. Come or don't."
"Every night I see it," {ally} says, buckling on {their} belt. "Every night. I'm not sitting another one out. Not for you, not for anyone. I'm going after {villain_short} now."

label: Talk {them} down. You will go together, and you will go ready.
result: {ally} stands a long time with {their} hand on the pack. Then {they} let{s} it fall. "Together," {they} say{s}. "Ready. Aye. But soon."
"You're right," {ally} says at last, and sits. "I'd only die, and it'd only laugh."
fail_result: {ally} hears you out, and shakes {their} head, and goes. You hear {their} steps on the road a long while in the dark.
"No," {ally} says. "You've had your chance to be quick about it." And {they} {are} gone.

label: Take the pack from {them}. {They} {are} not going anywhere.
result: You take it from {them}. For a moment you think {ally} will fight you. Then {they} sit{s} down, and will not look at you again that night.
{ally} lets you take the pack, and hates you for it, and stays.
fail_result: {ally} twists out of your grip and is gone into the dark, and you do not follow.
"Don't," {ally} says, and there is a knife in {their} hand. You let {them} go.

label: Let {them} go. It is {their} grief, not yours.
result: You stand aside. {ally} grips your arm once, hard, and goes.
"Thank you," {ally} says, of all things, and walks off into the dark towards {home}.

title: {ally}'s doubts
Second thoughts
Is it worth it?
text: {ally} has been slow on the road all day, and at the fire {they} say{s} it straight out: "I don't know that you can do this. I don't know that anyone can. I've {mine} to think of. Maybe I should go home while there's a home to go to."
"I keep thinking," {ally} says, not looking at you, "of what happens to {town} if we die out here. Nobody left. Nobody to warn them. I think I should go back."
{ally} counts the days on {their} fingers. "This long, and {villain_short} still out there. Tell me why I shouldn't go home. Tell me honestly."

label: Tell {them} what you have seen, and why you will win.
result: {ally} listens, and the doubt goes slowly out of {their} face. "All right," {they} say{s}. "All right. I'll see it through."
"Aye," {ally} says at last. "Put like that. Aye."
fail_result: {ally} hears you out, and is sorry, and is gone home in the morning.
"You believe it," {ally} says. "I can see that. I just don't." {They} leave{s} at first light.

label: Ask what is really frightening {them}.
result: It comes out at last, the real fear, and once it is said aloud it is smaller. {ally} stays, and is better company for it.
"It's not dying," {ally} says. "It's dying for nothing." You talk until the fire is out. {They} stay{s}.
fail_result: You guess wrong, and {ally} shuts up like a door. In the morning {they} {are} gone home.
"That's not it," {ally} says. "You don't understand. Never mind." At dawn {they} {are} gone.

label: Go home, then, with my thanks.
result: {ally} looks almost ashamed of how glad {they} {are}. "I'll tell them in {town} what you're doing," {they} say{s}. "I'll tell them right."

title: {ally} is taken
A rider from {town}
Gone in the night
text: A boy on a lathered pony finds you, from {patron}: {ally} has been taken in the night, dragged off towards {home}, and there was blood on the step.
Word comes from {town}, in {patron}'s own hand: {ally} is gone. Whatever {villain_short} keeps, it has {them} now.
A rider stops you on the road. "From {patron}," he says, and then: "It's {ally}. They came for {them} in the night. They took {them} up to {home}."

title: When it is over
{ally}'s choice
The last night
text: It is over. {ally} sits a long time by the fire, turning something over in {their} hands. "I came for {mine}," {they} say{s}. "That's done now. And I find I don't want to go home. Not yet. If you'll have me, I'll go where you go."

"I've been thinking," {ally} says, "what I'll do now. Go back to {town}, I suppose. Or." {They} look{s} at you. "Or not. I'd swear to you, if you'd take it. I've seen what you do. I'd sooner do it with you than sit at home."

{ally} kneels by the fire, which is not a thing {they} {have} ever done before, and holds out {their} blade hilt first. "You saw {mine} put right. I owe you that. I'd give you my oath, if you want it."

label: Take {ally}'s oath.
result: "Then that's that," {ally} says, and grins, the first time you have seen it. "Where to?"
You take the hilt. {ally} gets up looking taller than {they} did.
"Good," {ally} says. "Good. I'll not let you down."

label: Send {ally} home, with your thanks.
result: {ally} is disappointed, and hides it, and is glad, and hides that too. You part at the road to {town} as friends.
"Home, then," {ally} says. "Aye. Somebody should see to it." {They} clasp{s} your arm, and then {they} {are} gone.
{ally} nods slowly. "You're right. They'll need me there." {They} {are} gone at first light, with a wave from the bend in the road.
